Admission Officer
Queensland Royal Hospital

Re: Mrs. Julia Smith, 21 years old
Dear Sir/Madam,

I am writing to refer Mrs. Julia Smith, a 21 year old lady who has recently delivered her baby, for your       Comment [OET1]: new mother who has
                                                                                                                                  th
kind assessment. Kindly admit the baby in NICU.                                                                delivered in the 30 week of gestation


Please note, Julia was at 30 weeks of her first pregnancy when she delivered her baby. Although she            Comment [OET2]: is a visitor from Cyprus
has no previous hospital visits or vaccinations, she used to get monthly visits from her local midwife.        who is carrying no medical records
Regarding her family history, it is positive for diabetes, hypertension, stroke and inguinal hernia. Please    Comment [OET3]: had no ante-natal
note, Julia was at 30 weeks of her first pregnancy when she delivered her baby. Although she has no
previous hospital visits or vaccinations, she used to get monthly visits from her local midwife.

On 05/12/2021, Julia presented with severe episodic abdominal and back pain in addition to vaginal             Comment [OET4]: Today morning
bleeding and burst water bag. At 8:04 am, bloody show occurred with ruptured amniotic membranes and
strong uterine contractions every two minutes. Her cervical examination revealed six cm dilatation with
90% effacement, as well as station one head engagement. At that time her blood pressure was 140/90,            Comment [OET5]: Her
heart rate was 98/min and her baby heart sounds were audible. As a result of being in active labor,
delivery of the baby was planned while giving I.V. hydralazine, hydrochloride 5-10 mg every 15-20
minutes to control the blood pressure. At 8:40 am, her blood pressure and heart rate improved to 130/90        Comment [OET6]: had
and 80/min respectively, and CTG was stable. In addition to this cervical effacement progressed to 100%
and head engagement to 4+ with strong frequent uterine contractions. Therefore, hydralazine was
stopped. Finally at 9:10 am, baby was delivered with a weight of 4.1 kg. It is worth noting that mother is
stable with no vaginal lacerations.

Regarding Julia’s baby, at 9:11 am, his APGAR score was 5, he was not crying and he appeared cyanosed.         Comment [OET7]: ;
As a result, massage and back slaps were started which provoked his crying. He was kept on warmer with         Comment [OET8]: and received
nasal suctioning. At 9:16 am, his APGAR changed to seven; however, he is currently hypothermic and             Comment [OET9]: improved
cyanosed.

Based on the above findings, I believe Julia and her baby need immediate transfer to a hospital with NICU
for resuscitation by a pediatrician and management by obstetrician, respectively. Should you have any          Comment [OET10]: to be managed
queries, please do not hesitate to contact me.                                                                 Comment [OET11]: an

Yours sincerely,                                                                                               Comment [OET12]: faithfully
Doctor

                                    introduction.
                                 2. Always read and select case notes carefully.
                                 3. Avoid basic grammar errors.
                                 4. Improve choice of words.
                                 5. Improve coherence/paragraphing.
                                 6. Try to finish the letter in 200 words by writing information in
                                    brief wherever possible. Watch this video on word length:
